title: Middlebury vs Williams: tuition, size, location
summary: Middlebury College (Middlebury) versus Williams College (Williams). Also searched as Williams vs Middlebury. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Middlebury College and Williams College are both private nonprofit institutions, as indicated by their ownership code 2 in the College Scorecard. Middlebury College, located in Middlebury, has an undergraduate enrollment of 2,738 students, while Williams College in Williamstown enrolls 2,076 undergraduates. Tuition for in-state students at Middlebury is $67,600, slightly lower than Williams College's $68,560. These differences highlight variations in size, location, and cost between the two colleges.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: Middlebury College and Williams College have comparable tuition costs for both in-state and out-of-state students, with Middlebury charging $67,600 and Williams $68,560. Despite the similarity in tuition, the median debt for students who complete their degrees differs slightly, with Middlebury graduates carrying a median debt of $13,857 compared to Williams graduates at $12,761. These figures provide insight into the financial commitments associated with attending each institution.

In comparing Middlebury vs Williams, the tuition rates are nearly equivalent, reflecting their status as private nonprofit colleges. However, the variation in median debt among completers suggests differences in financial aid packages, student borrowing patterns, or other economic factors influencing student debt at each college.

sections.heading: Pick Middlebury if
paragraphs: Pick Middlebury College if you are seeking a private nonprofit institution with a highly selective admission process, as it has an admission rate of approximately 10.75%. sections.heading: Pick Williams if
paragraphs: Pick Williams College if you prefer a private nonprofit institution with an even more selective admission rate of 8.25%, compared to Middlebury College.
